research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; current YE March 2026 offence composition, coverage, trend, data-quality and outcome-timing controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Cifas reporting under Report Fraud
verified_claims: Cifas now shares all information reports that could amount to a crime
Cifas reports are classified as crimes when they meet Home Office Counting Rules
limitations: classification depends on HOCR and differs from the legacy subset supply

sources.name: UK Finance report treatment
verified_claims: UK Finance reports continue to be used as information reports supporting investigations and law enforcement
limitations: information reports are not automatically recorded crimes

sources.name: Police recorded crime local and timely role
verified_claims: police recorded crime is the main source for local crime statistics
it can provide timely insight into emerging trends and lower-volume well-recorded offences
limitations: it excludes unreported and unrecorded crime

sources.name: Police recorded crime coverage gap
verified_claims: police recorded crime excludes offences that are not reported or not recorded
limitations: long-term trends can be influenced by recording practice, police activity and public reporting

sources.name: May 2023 conduct-crime recording change
verified_claims: May 2023 recording-rule changes removed the requirement to record two crimes reported together with the same perpetrator when one was a conduct crime
the change reduced counts for offences often associated with conduct crimes such as malicious communications
limitations: the rule change creates a time-series discontinuity

sources.name: Alternative-offence outcome publication QA
verified_claims: outcomes 1a, 2a and 3a have been included in open data and summary tables since late 2023 after Home Office quality assurance
limitations: publication suitability does not identify the specific alternative offence charged

sources.name: Future diversionary caution
verified_claims: the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts framework proposed a Diversionary Caution as an upper-tier adult out-of-court resolution
limitations: the future framework depends on provisions coming into force

sources.name: Future community caution
verified_claims: the proposed framework includes a Community Caution as a lower-tier adult out-of-court resolution
limitations: the caution is part of a future framework, not a current outcome count

sources.name: Potential PND and warning discontinuation
verified_claims: the proposed out-of-court framework could discontinue Penalty Notices for Disorder and Cannabis or Khat Warnings
limitations: the relevant provisions had not necessarily come into force

sources.name: Outcome metrics user engagement
verified_claims: Home Office launched a user engagement exercise on aligning headline outcome metrics with policing investigative-performance measures
limitations: the exercise does not itself change the published statistics

sources.name: Victim-based charge median days
verified_claims: victim-based charge or summons outcomes took a median 40 days
this was one day lower than the previous year's 41 days
limitations: median timing varies substantially by offence type

sources.name: Robbery charge timing
verified_claims: robbery charge or summons timing decreased by 8 days from 67 to 59 days
limitations: the change is not a direct efficiency ranking

sources.name: Sexual offence charge timing
verified_claims: sexual offence charge or summons timing increased from 275 to 284 days
rape charge timing increased from 434 to 438 days
limitations: case complexity and cohort maturity affect timing

sources.name: Criminal damage charge timing
verified_claims: criminal damage and arson charge or summons decisions took a median 26 days
this was 5 days lower than the previous year
limitations: the metric does not control for offence mix

sources.name: Sexual offences still open
verified_claims: 26.3% of sexual offences remained open without an assigned outcome at year-end
limitations: the high open share contributes to an initially low charge rate
